description: "An Essay on Papal Infallibility" by John Sinclair is a theological discourse written in the mid-19th century. The book critically examines the doctrine of papal infallibility, a concept central to Roman Catholic belief, arguing against the notion that the Pope is a divinely appointed infallible authority in matters of faith.
